title: Ephemeral adminlet schema + run-rehearsal CLI for safe ops automation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Introduce a lightweight, typed 'adminlet' artifact and a CLI-driven rehearsal flow to let engineers rehearse, score, and safely execute atomic ops steps. An adminlet is a small, schema-defined operation (idempotent when possible) that captures inputs, required permissions, safety gates, and a simulated 'rehearsal' that produces a non-destructive trace. We will ship: (1) a protobuf-based adminlet schema with explicit versions and migration guidance; (2) a local CLI that performs static validation, runs a dry-run rehearsal against a sandbox environment, computes a trust_score from historical telemetry and rehearsal diffs, and optionally produces a signed execution token; (3) platform-side support for ephemeral RBAC tokens, audit provenance fields, and a replayable rehearsal store integrated with incident timelines.
acceptance_criteria: Define a v1 adminlet schema in proto with fields: id, version, input_schema, output_schema, required_permissions, safety_checks, estimated_impact, rollback_plan, and metadata
CLI 'adminlet run --rehearse' validates inputs, invokes sandbox rehearsal, and emits a rehearsal trace JSON with a computed trust_score and diff summary
Platform accepts signed execution tokens (short-lived) issued by the CLI; tokens carry adminlet id + input hash and expire in <= 30m
Rehearsal traces are persisted to rehearsal-store with linking to incident IDs and are queryable from Console (rehearsal tab)
Telemetry: emit events for rehearsal_start, rehearsal_finish, rehearsal_diff_size, trust_score, and execution_attempt
Unit and integration tests cover schema validation, rehearsal sandbox stubbing, token signing/verification, and audit-log generation
Internal pilot runbook: convert 5 common manual runbooks into adminlets and run 10 rehearsals without customer-facing regressions
tasks: Design: finalize proto schema and migration story (Ava)
Engine: implement CLI skeleton, validation, and token flow (Ravi)
Platform: add rehearsal-store API and ephemeral token verifier (Morgan)
Security: threat model + key rotation plan for signing keys (Sofia)
Telemetry: wire rehearsal metrics to staging Grafana dashboard (Jordan)
UX: Console rehearsal viewer + diff visualization hookup (Priya)
Pilot: migrate 5 runbooks and run pilot week; collect feedback and incidents
notes: Decision: use protobuf for adminlet contracts (reason: strong typing, stable binary compatibility, and easier client code generation across SDKs). Alternative JSON Schema rejected for v1 due to laxness around typed enums.
Trade-off: rehearsals in some cases will be best-effort (can't fully validate external side effects). We'll require a manual sign-off UI for high-impact adminlets (estimated_impact >= high).
Rollback plan: adminlet schema must include an explicit rollback_plan field; platform cannot auto-rollback arbitrary external systems, so docs will enforce documenting reversal steps.

Safety: rehearsals run in a per-customer sandbox namespace that mirrors resource metadata but replaces destructive API endpoints with no-ops; we'll instrument a 'diff harness' to surface changed vs expected outputs.
Instrumentation: trust_score computed from weighted factors: rehearsal_diff_size, historical_success_rate, operator_role_score, and recent incident correlation. We will iterate weights post-pilot.
Open question: whether to allow parameterized templating in inputs (e.g., env interpolation). For v1 we will only support literal inputs to avoid injection risk.
